title: Asian and Pacific Islander students make up 7.1% of Rye Neck Middle School enrollment for 2025-26
text:
During the 2025-26 school year, Rye Neck Middle School counted 24 Asian and Pacific Islander students, a decline of 27.3% from the prior year, according to the New York State Education Department .
Enrollment data indicated that the school served 339 students for 2025-26, with Asian and Pacific Islander students representing 7.1% of the total population, making them the third least represented group at the school.
Rye Neck Middle School is part of the Rye Neck Union Free School District, which has its main office in Mamaroneck.
Within the district’s four schools, F. E. Bellows Elementary School had the largest number of Asian and Pacific Islander students during the same period, enrolling 41 students.
New York is ranked second in the U.S. for K-12 public education spending , with per-student expenditures averaging $30,012—almost twice the national average of $16,526, according to the Education Data Initiative.
